title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Blackstone’s Jas Khaira on building the next generation of AI giants
slides: Can Blackstone's Jas Khaira spot the next AI giant?
He says most AI startups will fail.
But the winners share one weird trait.
Founders must prove real revenue, not hype.
Ask yourself: does your AI product survive scrutiny?
thread_text:
1. The One Trait That Wins

Blackstone's Jas Khaira says most AI startups will fail. The few that survive share a trait nobody talks about.

2. Why Startups Die

Khaira meets hundreds of founders. Most pitch vision and tech. He says that's exactly why they lose.

3. The Weird Trait

Winners prove real revenue from day one, not hype. That single focus separates them from the rest.

4. Revenue Is the Filter

Investors now ask for paying customers, not user growth. Founders who can't show it get cut fast.

5. Test Your Product

Take your AI product and ask: would a stranger pay for this today? If not, fix that first.

Most AI startups pitching to Blackstone will never see a check. Jas Khaira, who meets hundreds of founders, says vision and tech alone are why they lose.

The winners prove real revenue from day one, not user growth. Investors now want paying customers, and founders who can't show them get cut fast.

If you're building or publishing AI content, stop counting followers and start counting buyers. 💸 Your demo has to survive a stranger's wallet test.

Would someone pay for your AI product today? If not, that's your only priority. 🔍
